subject: Contract refresh: priority retainer & latency bands for expansion
messages:
From: Mark Delaney <mark.delaney@gridlane.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Contract refresh: priority retainer & latency bands for expansion

Hi Evelyn,

Quick one — GridLane is planning a Q4 product expansion that will increase inference volume ~3x starting in January. We're approaching our renewal window and want to explore a cleaner path that combines: a) a reserved capacity uplift, b) upgraded support (priority retainer / named on-call), and c) committed latency bands for our conversational endpoints.

High-level asks from my side:
- Dedicated reserved capacity to cover base traffic + 30% burst
- Priority retainer with 24/7 response for Sev1 incidents and a named escalation engineer
- Latency commitments: 95th < 200ms and 99th < 500ms for the primary model profile (we can share traces)
- Clear rollback/fallback plan if you need to change model variants during incidents

Can you send a short doc outlining options + rough pricing? Procurement (procurement@gridlane.com) will need contract & invoicing cadence too. Happy to jump on a call next week for a quick tech + commercial run-through.

Thanks,
Mark
Mark Delaney
Head of Product
GridLane

[attachment: customer-traffic-projections.xlsx]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Delaney <mark.delaney@gridlane.com>
Cc: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@gridlane.com>, procurement@gridlane.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract refresh: priority retainer & latency bands for expansion

Mark — thanks for the context and congrats on the product expansion. I've put together a short proposal attached (priority_retainer_summary.pdf) plus a technical latency-band mapping (latency_bands.xlsx). Key highlights: 

- Reserved capacity: commit to a dedicated pool sized for current baseline *plus* 30% burst. We can stage an incremental uplift phased over two months to smooth deployment risk.
- Support: Priority retainer with named escalation engineer, 15-minute pager for Sev1, 1-hour RM (response) for Sev2. Dedicated Slack channel and quarterly operational reviews.
- Latency SLOs: we commit to a 95th percentile token latency of <200ms and 99th <500ms for the agreed test profile and steady-state traffic patterns. Caveats and measurement windows are in the attachment (we must define the test profile and tracing hooks).
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a compatible quantized model variant and cross-region failover policy; we will document expected quality delta.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical calibration call — next Tue/Wed to validate the latency test profile (15–30m)
2) Procurement receives draft contract & invoice schedule (I attached a sample term sheet)
3) Pilot uplift window (60 days) with a follow-up ops review after 30 days

If that aligns, I can loop Ben for pricing and Lauren for the onboarding timeline. Thought I should include a working DocuSign link once we have final terms.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: priority_retainer_summary.pdf, latency_bands.xlsx

Specific asks:

Evelyn — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying points from procurement & infra before we lock terms: 

1) Procurement needs an invoice schedule that allows one annual payment or quarterly. Can you confirm your preferred cadence and whether we can push Net-60?
2) For the latency SLOs, does the measurement include tokenization/transform pre-processing time, or should we carve that out? We prefer SLOs measured from request entry to first token emitted at the model surface.
3) For the pilot uplift: we approve a 60-day pilot but ask for an option to scale down at day-30 if integration issues arise (with billing pro-rated).
4) Can you provide the contract redline (we started one on our side — attached as contract-redline-v1.pdf)?

If we can get those items resolved this week we can route for exec sign-off. Also: can you include the named escalation engineer's CV/linked profile and confirm the on-call calendar?

Best,
Nathan Lee
VP Engineering, GridLane
procurement@gridlane.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract refresh: priority retainer & latency bands for expansion — next steps

All — great alignment. Quick responses inline then next steps below: 

1) Invoice cadence: we support annual, quarterly, and monthly invoicing. Standard terms are Net-30; Net-60 is possible for enterprise customers with a small finance surcharge — I put Net-60 option in the redline suggestion.
2) Latency measurement: we will measure SLOs from request ingress at the public endpoint to first token out; preprocessing/tokenization is excluded per your ask — we'll include the exact measurement hook in the SLA appendix.
3) Pilot uplift: we agree to a 60-day pilot with a day-30 ops review and the option to scale down with pro-rated billing if unresolved integration issues remain. We'll document the rollback criteria in the pilot playbook.
4) Named escalation engineer: assigning Priya Natarajan as the primary escalation lead (CV linked in the onboarding packet); weekly on-call calendar and 15-minute pager window documented.

Attachments: I included the contract redline (our comments) and a draft DocuSign envelope to accelerate signatures. Once procurement confirms Net-60 acceptance, Ben will lock final pricing and I'll drop the DocuSign link.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Ben to confirm pricing matrix with pilot credit (ETA EOD today)
- Procurement to confirm invoicing cadence and Net-60 acceptability
- Schedule technical calibration call (Evelyn / GridLane infra / Redwood infra) for Wed 10/7 10:00am PT — Lauren will send calendar invite
- I will upload the onboarding packet and Priya's profile to the shared folder once Ben confirms pricing
